sources.density_kg_m3: judgment: quartz and feldspar, like granite without its mafic minerals; rounded to 10 kg/m³; set in P1-12; reviewed in P1-07 against the rock map and meridian cross-sections of pipeline_quick_16k and kept (STATUS.md, P1-07)
sources.erodibility: judgment, relative to granite: very coarse; cleavage and grain boundaries weaken it; bedrock ranked by rock strength: river incision scales roughly with tensile strength^-2 (Sklar & Dietrich 2001, Geology 29(12):1087–1090) and lithologic K contrasts span orders of magnitude (Stock & Montgomery 1999, JGR 104(B3):4983–4993); the strength-based contrast is compressed to its square root, so bedrock spans about 0.3–4; set in P1-12; reviewed in P1-07 against the rock map and meridian cross-sections of pipeline_quick_16k and kept (STATUS.md, P1-07)
sources.diffusivity: judgment, relative to granite: coarse granitic rock, like granite; hillslope transport coefficient D of Roering, Kirchner & Dietrich 1999 (WRR 35(3):853–870), used as a linear creep multiplier and scaled by how readily the rock makes mobile soil (soil production function, Heimsath et al. 1997, Nature 388:358–361): loose and friable classes 2–5, soft sedimentary 1.2–2, crystalline 0.5–1; set in P1-12; reviewed in P1-07 against the rock map and meridian cross-sections of pipeline_quick_16k and kept (STATUS.md, P1-07)
sources.vanilla_fallback: last fallback entry (MIC rock-tag README, Fallbacks table)
sources.stone_use: judgment (P1-28, Ben's hardness tiers 2026-10-01): huge feldspar and quartz crystals that cleave: strong in a wall, shatters when knapped

notes: Granitic pegmatite (LCT and NYF), host of lithium, tantalum, tin and rare-element ores.
